statement: Let n = len(nums). For a length-n integer list b, call b valid when b[i] >= nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n and the values b[0],...,b[n-1] are pairwise distinct. Define cost(b) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (b[i] - nums[i]). The function returns a result r, and r is the minimum of cost(b) over all valid b.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Also assume the promised 32-bit answer bound: the minimum number of one-step increments needed to make all values of nums pairwise distinct is at most 2^31 - 1.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Also assume the promised 32-bit answer bound: the minimum number of one-step increments needed to make all values of nums pairwise distinct is at most 2^31 - 1.

statement: Let c(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = v, for integer v; only finitely many c(v) are nonzero. The function returns a result r, and r >= sum over all integers v of c(v)*(c(v)-1)/2.

statement: Let a be a nondecreasing rearrangement of nums, so a[0] <= a[1] <= ... <= a[n-1]. Define y[0] = a[0], and for 1 <= i < n define y[i] = max(a[i], y[i-1] + 1). Then the function returns a result r, and r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (y[i] - a[i]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Also assume the promised 32-bit answer bound.

statement: The function returns results r for nums and r_sub for sub, and r_sub <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Also assume the promised 32-bit answer bound. Let sub be any slice of length m with 1 <= m <= n for which there is an injection phi from {0,...,m-1} to {0,...,n-1} such that sub[j] = nums[phi(j)] for every 0 <= j < m. Assume sub also satisfies the same constraints and answer bound.
